overall_structure.value: Multiphase microstructure of nano-bainitic steel S3 after austenitizing at 1220 °C and austempering at 270 °C: a bainitic ferrite (αb) matrix with retained austenite (γr) at lath boundaries (partly blocky/sluggish γr in transformation-free micro-regions) plus an unavoidable residual polygonal ferrite (αp) fraction of 8.2 %, together with (Fe,M)xCy precipitates located near γr–bainitic ferrite boundaries and nanoscale non-stoichiometric L12-type κ-carbide embedded in the matrix.

number_of_phases.value: ≥4 (bainitic ferrite, retained austenite, polygonal ferrite, (Fe,M)xCy carbides; plus nanoscale κ-carbide and AlN)

morphology.value: nano-bainitic laths; true lamellar thickness Lt(t) = 40 nm (SD 10 nm); lenticular sheaves with impingement of bainite sheaves; higher SD at higher TB indicates nB Type 1 and Type 2 alongside blocky γr

blocky γr regions between bainitic sheaves; partially decomposed sluggish γr in some micro-regions; in S3 at 270 °C the higher average εγ (0.54 %) versus ferritic phases (0.33 %) indicates pronounced strain partitioning and dislocation accumulation in the metastable γr

interaction_type.value: strain partitioning / dislocation accumulation in retained austenite

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: At 270 °C the phase-resolved microstrain differed markedly between γr and bainitic ferrite (εγ: 0.54 % vs. εα: 0.33 %), consistent with pronounced strain partitioning; the significantly higher ε in the metastable γr indicates pronounced dislocation accumulation, leading to the formation of highly brittle phase boundaries and potential stress-spiking regions, which explains the severe drop in elongation to 2.4 %.

interaction_type.value: carbon partitioning / bainite growth stalling at αp–austenite interfaces

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: αp can serve as nucleation sites for bainitic transformation, but its low C solubility leads to significant C-partitioning into the adjacent austenite (C-enrichment), locally stabilizing the austenite and increasing the energy barrier around αp plates. Initial nucleation was observed at αp–austenite interfaces, but bainite growth could not propagate and stalled at many sites, leaving transformation-free regions that required much longer holding times (25,200 s incomplete; 43,200 s near-complete).

phase_evolution.value: During austempering at 270 °C of S3: bainite nucleates at αp–austenite interfaces but growth stalls; C-enrichment around αp stabilizes adjacent austenite, producing partially decomposed sluggish γr and transformation-free regions; only a prolonged duration (~43,000 s) achieves near-complete bainitic transformation.

interface_notes.value: (Fe,M)xCy precipitates are located near the γr–bainitic ferrite phase boundaries; highly brittle phase boundaries and stress-spiking regions form because of the imbalanced dislocation distribution; Si entrapped in the Fe-based carbide lattice and Mo enhance precipitate stability, inhibiting void formation.

unmapped_findings: Chemical composition of steel S3 (wt.%): C 1.05, Al 8.08, Mn 1.00, Si 0.30, Mo 0.50, B 0.0039; Ni and Ti not added (Table 1; Al content highest of the studied steels).
S3 austenitizing temperatures: MatCalc ferrite-free TA = 1177 °C; measured TA = broadened transition without a unique value; applied TA = 1220 °C (Table 2 / Fig. 2).

S3 martensite start temperature Ms = 258 °C measured by cooling dilatometry after austenitizing at 1220 °C — the lowest Ms among the studied steels, consistent with extended κ-carbide dissolution and ferrite retention facilitating local carbon partitioning into austenite.

S3 carbide-dissolution temperature Tcd ≈ 1103 °C from MatCalc equilibrium phase-fraction simulation; the simulated ferrite-free TA of ~1177 °C could not be fully achieved in practice (residual αp 8.2 % at 1220 °C).

S3 product of strength and elongation (PSE) ≈ 3480 MPa·% (≈ 3.5 GPa·%) at TB 270 °C (UTS 1450 MPa, El 2.4 %) and ~11,150 MPa·% at TB 350 °C (UTS 1360 MPa, El 8.2 %) — the lowest PSE of the study at 270 °C.

S3 transformation kinetics: Bt ≈ 43,000 s at TB 270 °C (incubation 120 s, slow bainite growth period ~3000 s) and Bt ≈ 14,000 s at TB 350 °C (incubation 140 s, slow growth period ~1500 s); the slow transformation is attributed to C-enrichment and stabilization of austenite around polygonal ferrite.

Bainitic transformation times of the comparison steels for context: S5 (fastest, Bt 700–1000 s), S1/S2 (Bt 1600–4000 s), S4 Ti-microalloyed (Bt 3000–3500 s); S3 with ~8 wt.% Al is the slowest (Bt 14,000–43,000 s); small Ni addition (0.78 wt.% in S4 and S5) did not affect transformation time.

Hardness values reported in Fig. 7 for the eleven TA/TB conditions (left to right: 464, 497, 465, 500, 443, 457, 464, 479, 467, 459, 493 HV30); the S3, TA: 1220 °C, TB: 270 °C condition corresponds to 457 HV30, consistent with the statement that hardness (450–500 HV30) is higher at lower TB except for S4.

SEM/EDX of S3 identified, besides (Fe,M)xCy, an AlN particle (Spec.4) in the 270 °C condition, and Al contents within particles were essentially absent, indicating a nucleation-driven (not spinodal) formation mechanism.

κ-carbide (E21-type stoichiometric perovskite) was not directly examined microscopically in S3; its absence of observable structures is attributed to the limited Mn content (≈1 wt.%), with remaining κ-carbides presumed to exist as nanoscale, embedded, non-stoichiometric L12-type structures.
